name: eBay used Intel Arc B580 12GB consumer cards
price_basis: USED / Pre-Owned, bare PCIe consumer card, as-is. $290.00 = Acer Nitro Intel Arc B580 12GB 'Used condition, Tested'. Observed used B580 band: $290.00-$499.00 (Sparkle 12GB $304.00, GUNNIR Index $319.00, ASRock Challenger $319.99, Intel Limited Edition $339.00, ASRock Steel Legend $450-$500). Captured 2026-10-03. No warranty. ASKING prices.
notes: The decision-relevant finding here is NEGATIVE and worth recording: the used market for B580 is thin (only 13 genuine B580 cards in the used-filtered result set) AND used is not cheaper than new. eBay's own price histogram for used B580 puts 7 items in $300-400, 4 in $400-500, 1 in $250-300 - and the same card sells NEW at $329.99 through Newegg. Buying used Intel consumer silicon is therefore a bad trade at these price points; see the Newegg Refreshed record for the refurb tier that actually undercuts new. Second observation: adjacent Arc parts show a coherent used ladder worth noting for inference builds - Arc Pro B70 32GB at $1,329.00, Arc Pro B50 16GB at $449.99-$690.00 (including one with a third-party single-slot cooler at $599.00/$690.00, which is the retrofit route to density), Arc B570 10GB at $244.99-$375.00, Arc A750 8GB at $170.00. The B50 16GB at $449.99-$500.00 is the genuinely interesting number: 16GB of GDDR6 workstation silicon for under the price of a used 4090.
